questions.stem: On Type anatomy terms: a designer reviewing a film festival program booklet notices that a designer calls the enclosed white area inside a letter a stem. Which correction to the terminology is accurate?

options.text: The enclosed area is a counter rather than a stem of the letter
A stem is the curved stroke that encloses the white space
options.misconception: swaps the names of the stroke and the enclosed space

options.text: The counter is the main vertical stroke of the letterform
options.misconception: reverses the meanings of counter and stem completely

options.text: These parts of letters have no agreed names in typography
options.misconception: denies the well-established vocabulary of type anatomy

questions.explanation: In type anatomy a counter is the enclosed or partly enclosed white area of a letter, while a stem is a principal straight stroke. Naming parts precisely lets designers discuss shapes without ambiguity, so calling the counter a stem is simply the wrong term.
questions.hint: Which term names the white hole in a letter such as the lowercase o?
